claim: An mRNA expression time course of zebrafish development was produced across 18 time points from 1 cell to 5 days post-fertilisation.
source: We have produced an mRNA expression time course of zebrafish development across 18 time points from 1 cell to 5 days post-fertilisation sampling individual and pools of embryos.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and describes the experimental design.

claim: The study used poly(A) pulldown stranded RNA-seq and a 3′ end transcript counting method.
source: Using poly(A) pulldown stranded RNA-seq and a 3′ end transcript counting method we characterise temporal expression profiles of 23,642 genes.
evidence: The methods used are explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: Temporal expression profiles of 23,642 genes were characterized.
source: Using poly(A) pulldown stranded RNA-seq and a 3′ end transcript counting method we characterise temporal expression profiles of 23,642 genes.
evidence: The number of genes characterized is explicitly stated.

claim: 5024 unnamed genes were associated with distinct developmental time points through temporal and functional transcript co-variance.
source: We identify temporal and functional transcript co-variance that associates 5024 unnamed genes with distinct developmental time points.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: Over 100 previously uncharacterised zinc finger domain containing genes located on the long arm of chromosome 4 are expressed in a sharp peak during zygotic genome activation.
source: Specifically, a class of over 100 previously uncharacterised zinc finger domain containing genes, located on the long arm of chromosome 4, is expressed in a sharp peak during zygotic genome activation.
evidence: This specific finding about zinc finger genes is stated in the abstract.

claim: The data reveal new genes and transcripts.
source: In addition, the data reveal new genes and transcripts, differential use of exons and previously unidentified 3′ ends across development, new primary microRNAs and temporal divergence of gene paralogues generated in the teleost genome duplication.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as one of the findings in the abstract.

claim: The data reveal differential use of exons across development.
source: In addition, the data reveal new genes and transcripts, differential use of exons and previously unidentified 3′ ends across development, new primary microRNAs and temporal divergence of gene paralogues generated in the teleost genome duplication.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as one of the findings.

claim: Previously unidentified 3′ ends across development were revealed.
source: In addition, the data reveal new genes and transcripts, differential use of exons and previously unidentified 3′ ends across development, new primary microRNAs and temporal divergence of gene paralogues generated in the teleost genome duplication.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding.

claim: New primary microRNAs were identified.
source: In addition, the data reveal new genes and transcripts, differential use of exons and previously unidentified 3′ ends across development, new primary microRNAs and temporal divergence of gene paralogues generated in the teleost genome duplication.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding.

claim: Temporal divergence of gene paralogues generated in the teleost genome duplication was observed.
source: In addition, the data reveal new genes and transcripts, differential use of exons and previously unidentified 3′ ends across development, new primary microRNAs and temporal divergence of gene paralogues generated in the teleost genome duplication.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding.

claim: The data can be browsed and downloaded at Expression Atlas and Ensembl.
source: To make this dataset a useful baseline reference, the data can be browsed and downloaded at Expression Atlas and Ensembl.
evidence: The availability of the data is explicitly stated.

claim: Zebrafish possesses high morphological and genomic conservation with humans.
source: The zebrafish is a unique vertebrate model system as it possesses high morphological and genomic conservation with humans, but also experimental tractability of embryogenesis otherwise only found in invertebrate model organisms such as Drosophila melanogaster or Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of zebrafish.

claim: Zebrafish has experimental tractability of embryogenesis otherwise only found in invertebrate model organisms such as Drosophila melanogaster or Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: The zebrafish is a unique vertebrate model system as it possesses high morphological and genomic conservation with humans, but also experimental tractability of embryogenesis otherwise only found in invertebrate model organisms such as Drosophila melanogaster or Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of zebrafish.

claim: Zebrafish features such as very large numbers of offspring, ex vivo development and embryonic translucency have enabled comprehensive forward and reverse genetic screens.
source: Features such as very large numbers of offspring, ex vivo development and embryonic translucency have enabled comprehensive forward and reverse genetic screens (Amsterdam et al., 1999; Driever et al., 1996; Haffter et al., 1996; Kettleborough et al., 2013; Moens et al., 2008; Varshney et al., 2015) as well as high-throughput drug discovery approaches (Murphey et al., 2006; North et al., 2007; Peterson et al., 2000; Peterson et al., 2004; Stern et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Zebrafish features have enabled high-throughput drug discovery approaches.
source: Features such as very large numbers of offspring, ex vivo development and embryonic translucency have enabled comprehensive forward and reverse genetic screens (Amsterdam et al., 1999; Driever et al., 1996; Haffter et al., 1996; Kettleborough et al., 2013; Moens et al., 2008; Varshney et al., 2015) as well as high-throughput drug discovery approaches (Murphey et al., 2006; North et al., 2007; Peterson et al., 2000; Peterson et al., 2004; Stern et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Zebrafish has a high quality genome only comparable in vertebrates to mouse and human.
source: Together with a high quality genome (Howe et al., 2013b) only comparable in vertebrates to mouse and human, this has led to many important discoveries in areas such as zygotic genome activation (ZGA; Lee et al., 2013), blood stem cell biology (Bertrand et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010), and findings directly affecting human health (Li et al., 2015; Tobin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation and comparison to other model organisms.

claim: The first baseline expression study in zebrafish was conducted by Mathavan et al. (2005) using microarrays.
source: The first baseline expression study in zebrafish was conducted by Mathavan et al. (2005) using microarrays.
evidence: This is stated with a citation.

claim: Mathavan et al. (2005) profiled the expression of 14,904 genes across 12 time points from unfertilised egg to 2 days post-fertilisation.
source: This profiled the expression of 14,904 genes across 12 time points from unfertilised egg to 2 days post-fertilisation (dpf).
evidence: This describes the scope of the Mathavan et al. study.

claim: A total of 18 developmental time points were sampled in this study.
source: We sampled a total of 18 developmental time points in this study (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Four time points are before or at the onset of zygotic transcription.
source: Four time points are before or at the onset of zygotic transcription, four during gastrulation, three during somitogenesis, three during prim stages – 24, 30 and 36 hr post-fertilisation (hpf) – and every 24 hr from 2 to 5 dpf.
evidence: This describes the temporal distribution of sampling points.

claim: Four time points were sampled during gastrulation.
source: Four time points are before or at the onset of zygotic transcription, four during gastrulation, three during somitogenesis, three during prim stages – 24, 30 and 36 hr post-fertilisation (hpf) – and every 24 hr from 2 to 5 dpf.
evidence: This describes the temporal distribution of sampling points.

claim: Three time points were sampled during somitogenesis.
source: Four time points are before or at the onset of zygotic transcription, four during gastrulation, three during somitogenesis, three during prim stages – 24, 30 and 36 hr post-fertilisation (hpf) – and every 24 hr from 2 to 5 dpf.
evidence: This describes the temporal distribution of sampling points.

claim: At each time point, five biological replicates of pools of 12 embryos were collected.
source: At each time point, five biological replicates of pools of 12 embryos were collected and we obtained an average of 3.8 million reads per sample (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: An average of 3.8 million reads per sample was obtained.
source: At each time point, five biological replicates of pools of 12 embryos were collected and we obtained an average of 3.8 million reads per sample (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequencing.

claim: The number of genes detected rises steadily as development proceeds.
source: The number of genes detected rises steadily as development proceeds and a wider range of genes are expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The reduced number of detected genes during gastrulation is most likely caused by degradation of maternal mRNAs.
source: The reduced number of detected genes during gastrulation is most likely caused by degradation of maternal mRNAs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on biological knowledge.

claim: The distribution of expression levels is initially bimodal, with one peak at very low levels and another at much higher levels.
source: The distribution of expression levels (TPM, transcripts per million) is initially bimodal, with one peak at very low levels and another at much higher levels, and becomes more normally distributed as the embryo develops (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary files 2–3).
evidence: This describes the distribution pattern observed in the data.

claim: The distribution of expression levels becomes more normally distributed as the embryo develops.
source: The distribution of expression levels (TPM, transcripts per million) is initially bimodal, with one peak at very low levels and another at much higher levels, and becomes more normally distributed as the embryo develops (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary files 2–3).
evidence: This describes the change in distribution pattern over development.

claim: RNA-seq on homogeneous populations of cells produces a bimodal distribution whereas the distribution becomes more unimodal when heterogeneous samples are sequenced.
source: This pattern is consistent with the observation that RNA-seq on homogeneous populations of cells produces a bimodal distribution whereas the distribution becomes more unimodal when heterogeneous samples are sequenced (Hebenstreit et al., 2011), which fits well with the cells of the embryo being very similar at early stages and becoming more differentiated over time.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hebenstreit et al., 2011.

claim: The cells of the embryo are very similar at early stages and become more differentiated over time.
source: This pattern is consistent with the observation that RNA-seq on homogeneous populations of cells produces a bimodal distribution whereas the distribution becomes more unimodal when heterogeneous samples are sequenced (Hebenstreit et al., 2011), which fits well with the cells of the embryo being very similar at early stages and becoming more differentiated over time.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on known developmental biology.

claim: 83.0% of genes detected at dome stage at 1 TPM or above have promoter regions that overlap with an H3K4me3 peak.
source: Of the 12,950 genes detected at 1 TPM or above at dome, 10,747 (83.0%) of the promoter regions (1000 bp upstream to 200 bp downstream of the annotated transcription start site) overlap with an H3K4me3 peak, whereas only 10.7% (633/5930) of the promoters of genes that are not expressed (0 TPM in all samples at that stage) overlap (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing RNA-seq data with ChIP-seq data.

claim: Only 10.7% of the promoters of genes that are not expressed at dome stage overlap with an H3K4me3 peak.
source: Of the 12,950 genes detected at 1 TPM or above at dome, 10,747 (83.0%) of the promoter regions (1000 bp upstream to 200 bp downstream of the annotated transcription start site) overlap with an H3K4me3 peak, whereas only 10.7% (633/5930) of the promoters of genes that are not expressed (0 TPM in all samples at that stage) overlap (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing RNA-seq data with ChIP-seq data.

claim: At prim-5 (24 hpf), 64.8% of expressed genes have a corresponding H3K4me3 peak.
source: Similarly, at prim-5 (24 hpf) 64.8% (9741/15,044) of expressed genes have a corresponding peak, but only 4.9% (236/4845) of genes that are not expressed.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing RNA-seq data with ChIP-seq data.

claim: At prim-5, only 4.9% of genes that are not expressed have a corresponding H3K4me3 peak.
source: Similarly, at prim-5 (24 hpf) 64.8% (9741/15,044) of expressed genes have a corresponding peak, but only 4.9% (236/4845) of genes that are not expressed.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparing RNA-seq data with ChIP-seq data.

claim: The lower overlap of expressed genes with H3K4me3 peaks at prim-5 compared to dome is probably due to higher differentiation and tissue-restricted gene expression.
source: The overlap of expressed genes at this later stage is lower than at dome. However, this is probably due to the higher differentiation and therefore tissue-restricted gene expression in embryos at prim-5.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on biological reasoning.

claim: Whole embryo H3K4me3 ChIP-seq is not as sensitive as RNA-seq in detecting spatially restricted gene expression.
source: Whole embryo H3K4me3 ChIP-seq is not as sensitive as RNA-seq in detecting spatially restricted gene expression as it interrogates a small stretch of genomic sequence that carries the mark in only a subset of cells.
evidence: This is a methodological interpretation.

claim: Principal component analysis shows close clustering of biological replicates.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) shows close clustering of biological replicates and a smooth transition from one stage to another through developmental time (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Principal component analysis shows a smooth transition from one stage to another through developmental time.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) shows close clustering of biological replicates and a smooth transition from one stage to another through developmental time (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The first six principal components explain over 90% of the variance in the data.
source: The first six principal components (PCs) explain over 90% of the variance in the data (Figure 1—figure supplement 2); the first component accounts for 58.2% of the observed variation.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from PCA.

claim: The first principal component accounts for 58.2% of the observed variation.
source: The first six principal components (PCs) explain over 90% of the variance in the data (Figure 1—figure supplement 2); the first component accounts for 58.2% of the observed variation.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from PCA.

claim: PC6 has a clear spike of expression which starts at the 1000 cell stage (3 hpf) and peaks at dome (4.3 hpf) coinciding with the start of zygotic transcription.
source: The other patterns are more complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) although PC6 has a clear spike of expression, which starts at the 1000 cell stage (3 hpf) and peaks at dome (4.3 hpf) coinciding with the start of zygotic transcription.
evidence: This is stated and shown in the figure.

claim: The data are available through the European Nucleotide Archive.
source: The primary sequence is available from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA, http://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena), but importantly has also been interpreted for immediate user-friendly access.
evidence: This states where the data can be accessed.

claim: Pre-computed count profiles (TPM or FPKM) are available to search/browse at Expression Atlas.
source: Pre-computed count profiles (TPM or FPKM) are available to search/browse at Expression Atlas (http://www.ebi.ac.uk/gxa/experiments/E-ERAD-475)(Petryszak et al., 2016), allowing comparison of the expression profiles of multiple genes across the entire time course (Figure 2A).
evidence: This states where processed data can be accessed.

claim: Expression Atlas is searchable by gene/allele name, Ensembl ID and Gene Ontology (GO) terms.
source: This is searchable by gene/allele name, Ensembl ID and Gene Ontology (GO) terms.
evidence: This describes the search functionality of Expression Atlas.

claim: The data are viewable in Ensembl as separate stage-specific selectable tracks along with one merged track.
source: The data are also viewable in Ensembl as separate stage-specific selectable tracks along with one merged track (http://www.ensembl.org/Danio_rerio).
evidence: This describes how the data are displayed in Ensembl.

claim: 23,642 genes are detectable in this time course (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage).
source: Of the 23,642 detectable genes in this time course (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage), 5024 are genes with automatically generated names (often derived from clone IDs) such as zgc:* and si:ch*.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: 5024 genes have automatically generated names such as zgc:* and si:ch*.
source: Of the 23,642 detectable genes in this time course (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage), 5024 are genes with automatically generated names (often derived from clone IDs) such as zgc:* and si:ch*.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: At dome and gastrula stages, the proportion of unnamed genes is nearly twice as high (32.9–42.2%) as at other stages (18.2–28.6%).
source: Interestingly, at dome and gastrula stages, the proportion of these unnamed genes is nearly twice as high (32.9–42.2%) as at other stages (18.2–28.6%; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the data.

claim: BioLayout Express3D software was used to cluster and visualise the dataset.
source: To get smaller clusters that are more likely to contain biologically related genes, we used the BioLayout Express3D software (http://www.biolayout.org/) (Theocharidis et al., 2009) to cluster and visualise the dataset (Figure 3C).
evidence: This describes the method used for clustering.

claim: The Markov Cluster Algorithm (MCL) was used to find strongly connected components within the graph.
source: It then uses the Markov Cluster Algorithm (MCL, Enright et al., 2002; van Dongen, 2000) to find strongly connected components within the graph (Supplementary files 4–5).
evidence: This describes the clustering algorithm used.

claim: The clustering produces 254 clusters.
source: This produces 254 clusters, the vast majority of which (238/254) have fewer than 100 genes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: 238 out of 254 clusters have fewer than 100 genes.
source: This produces 254 clusters, the vast majority of which (238/254) have fewer than 100 genes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: Cluster 3 contains genes that are maternally supplied and then degraded.
source: For example, cluster 3 contains genes that are maternally supplied and then degraded and cluster 5 genes are not expressed until the last time points in the study.
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of a specific cluster.

claim: Cluster 5 genes are not expressed until the last time points in the study.
source: For example, cluster 3 contains genes that are maternally supplied and then degraded and cluster 5 genes are not expressed until the last time points in the study.
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of a specific cluster.

claim: Cluster 2 has genes that accumulate after the 2 cell stage, but before the onset of zygotic transcription.
source: Cluster 2 has genes that accumulate after the 2 cell stage, but before the onset of zygotic transcription (Figure 3C).
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of a specific cluster.

claim: Genes whose abundance changes before ZGA have been identified before and were shown to be regulated by the control of polyadenylation.
source: Genes whose abundance changes before ZGA have been identified before (Mathavan et al., 2005) and were shown to be regulated by the control of polyadenylation (Aanes et al., 2011; Harvey et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: 70 of the BioLayout clusters have significant GO enrichments (adjusted p-value<0.05).
source: 70 of the clusters have significant GO enrichments (adjusted p-value<0.05) and 17 have significant ZFA enrichments.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from enrichment analysis.

claim: 17 of the BioLayout clusters have significant ZFA enrichments.
source: 70 of the clusters have significant GO enrichments (adjusted p-value<0.05) and 17 have significant ZFA enrichments.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from enrichment analysis.

claim: Cluster 27 contains a large number of homeobox transcription factors (including fox, hox, irx and nkx gene families) that are expressed from 1 to 4 somites onwards.
source: For example, cluster 27 contains a large number of homeobox transcription factors (including fox, hox, irx and nkx gene families) that are expressed from 1 to 4 somites onwards and is associated with GO terms for transcription and development (Figure 3D).
evidence: This describes the content and expression pattern of a specific cluster.

claim: Clusters 36 and 49 have two peaks of expression and contain complement, clotting factor genes and serpins.
source: Clusters 36 and 49 have two peaks of expression and contain complement, clotting factor genes and serpins.
evidence: This describes the content and expression pattern of specific clusters.

claim: Clusters 36 and 49 have enrichments for terms related to blood clotting.
source: Both clusters have enrichments for the terms related to blood clotting (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from enrichment analysis.

claim: Cluster 30 contains well known developmental regulators such as admp, chd and fzd8b.
source: Notably, there are clusters that have stage-specific expression profiles, but no GO or ZFA enrichments (e.g. Cluster 30, Figure 3D). This cluster contains well known developmental regulators such as admp, chd and fzd8b and a large proportion of unnamed genes (10/42).
evidence: This describes the content of a specific cluster.

claim: Cluster 30 contains a large proportion of unnamed genes (10/42).
source: This cluster contains well known developmental regulators such as admp, chd and fzd8b and a large proportion of unnamed genes (10/42).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation about cluster composition.

claim: GO analysis on genes not present in the heatmap produces enrichments for terms related to apoptosis and the adaptive immune system.
source: GO analysis on the genes which are not present in the heatmap in Figure 3A (0 TPM in at least one sample for all stages) produces enrichments for terms related to apoptosis and the adaptive immune system with B-cell related terms such as B cell receptor signalling, immunoglobulin production and antigen processing and presentation (Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The adaptive immune system does not fully develop in zebrafish until 3 weeks post-fertilisation.
source: These fit well with the observation that the adaptive immune system does not fully develop in zebrafish until 3 weeks post-fertilisation (Lam et al., 2004; Trede et al., 2004; Willett et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Four clusters (clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135) have more chromosome 4 genes than would be expected by chance given the size of the clusters.
source: This identifies four clusters (clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135) with more chromosome 4 genes than would be expected by chance given the size of the clusters (Table 1).
evidence: This is a result from statistical testing.

claim: 153 out of 168 chromosome 4 genes within clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135 are predicted to encode proteins with ZnF domains.
source: Most of the chromosome 4 genes (153/168) within these clusters are predicted to encode proteins with ZnF domains (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from annotation analysis.

claim: The unnamed genes within clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135 represent on average 30.6% of the unnamed genes assigned to gastrula stages.
source: The unnamed genes within these clusters represent on average 30.6% of the unnamed genes assigned to gastrula stages in the maximum-stage groupings.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: The expression profiles of ZnF genes have a burst of expression from dome to 75% epiboly (4.3–8 hpf).
source: The expression profiles of these ZnF genes have a burst of expression from dome to 75% epiboly (4.3–8 hpf) and several begin to be expressed at the 128- and 1000 cell stages (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This describes the expression pattern observed in the data.

claim: Several ZnF genes begin to be expressed at the 128- and 1000 cell stages.
source: The expression profiles of these ZnF genes have a burst of expression from dome to 75% epiboly (4.3–8 hpf) and several begin to be expressed at the 128- and 1000 cell stages (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This describes the expression pattern observed in the data.

claim: Cluster 23 has a particularly sharp peak with a very large increase from the 1000 cell stage to dome and an almost equal decrease from dome to 50% epiboly.
source: Cluster 23 has a particularly sharp peak with a very large increase from the 1000 cell stage to dome and an almost equal decrease from dome to 50% epiboly.
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of a specific cluster.

claim: The ZnF genes are co-ordinately expressed at the onset of zygotic transcription.
source: This suggests that these ZnF genes are co-ordinately expressed at the onset of zygotic transcription.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the expression patterns observed.

claim: Of the 311 NLR genes present in the Ensembl version 85 genebuild, 148 have expression (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage) during this time course.
source: Of the 311 NLR genes present in the Ensembl version 85 genebuild, 148 have expression (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage) during this time course and they are not expressed in the same pattern as the ZnF genes (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: NLR genes are not expressed in the same pattern as the ZnF genes.
source: Of the 311 NLR genes present in the Ensembl version 85 genebuild, 148 have expression (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage) during this time course and they are not expressed in the same pattern as the ZnF genes (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the data.

claim: Only 9 of the NLR genes are assigned to a BioLayout cluster.
source: Only 9 of them are assigned to a BioLayout cluster.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: 62 chromosomal regions with co-expressed genes were identified.
source: This identified 62 regions (Supplementary file 9) including the hoxda cluster.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: The identified chromosomal regions include the hoxda cluster.
source: This identified 62 regions (Supplementary file 9) including the hoxda cluster.
evidence: This is a specific example from the results.

claim: There are several more groups of genes containing zinc finger domains in smaller regions on chromosomes 3, 15 and 22.
source: There are several more groups of genes containing zinc finger domains, in smaller regions on chromosomes 3, 15 and 22.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: For 26 out of 62 chromosomal regions, the homologous genes maintain their physical co-localisation when compared to the mouse and human genomes.
source: For some of the regions (26/62), when compared to the mouse and human genomes, the homologous genes maintain their physical co-localisation.
evidence: This is a result from comparative genomics analysis.

claim: Most chromosomal regions have been split up into two or three regions in mouse and human genomes, suggesting that there is no selective pressure on maintaining synteny.
source: However most of them have been split up into two or three regions, suggesting that there is no selective pressure on maintaining synteny (Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparative genomics data.

claim: Teleost fish underwent a third round of whole genome duplication compared to the two rounds of tetrapods.
source: Teleost fish underwent a third round of whole genome duplication compared to the two rounds of tetrapods (Meyer and Schartl, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: A list of 2929 one-to-one teleost-specific paralogous gene pairs with expression in the data was produced.
source: To investigate whether we can see this in our data, which has only stage and not tissue specificity information, we produced a list of one-to-one teleost-specific paralogous pairs using data from Ensembl (2929 gene pairs with expression in our data;>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage. Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This describes the dataset used for analysis.

claim: The distribution of correlation coefficients between paralogous pairs is skewed to high positive correlations when compared to a random sample of gene pairs.
source: The distribution of the correlation coefficients is skewed to high positive correlations when compared to a random sample of gene pairs of similar size (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a result from statistical analysis.

claim: 50% of the paralogous pair distribution has a correlation coefficient below 0.45.
source: Despite this skew, there is a significant proportion of the distribution with low or negative correlation coefficients, suggesting that this may represent a set of genes whose expression patterns have diverged (50% of the distribution is below 0.45).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: There are 683 paralogous gene pairs where there is anatomical expression information for both genes.
source: There are 683 gene pairs where there is anatomical expression information for both genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: For 83.7% of paralogous pairs with anatomical expression information, the intersection of stage ID and anatomy term pairs is less than 50%.
source: For each pair, we counted up the intersection of all the pairs of stage ID and anatomy term that make up the expression annotations. For the pairs studied, 83.7% (572 pairs) have an intersection of less than 50%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: GO analysis shows an enrichment for terms related to neural and muscle development in paralogous pairs.
source: GO analysis shows an enrichment for terms related to neural and muscle development (Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Neural terms are already enriched in the whole set of 3144 one-to-one paralogue pairs.
source: Neural terms are already enriched in the whole set of 3144 one-to-one paralogue pairs, but that enrichment becomes even greater when the gene set is limited to the highly correlated paralogue pairs (Pearson coefficient >0.9).
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Negatively correlated paralogous pairs (Pearson coefficient <−0.5) show limited enrichments.
source: By contrast, negatively correlated pairs (Pearson coefficient <−0.5) show limited enrichments.
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Temporal divergence of paralogous pairs is mirrored by greater diversity of GO annotations which leads to reduced term enrichment.
source: This suggests that temporal divergence is mirrored by greater diversity of GO annotations which in turn leads to reduced term enrichment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the enrichment analysis results.

claim: The Ensembl genebuild pipeline contains a procedure to build gene models from RNA-seq data and incorporate these models into the genebuild.
source: The Ensembl genebuild pipeline contains a procedure to build gene models from RNA-seq data and incorporate these models into the genebuild (Collins et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The data have been used by Ensembl to produce an updated gene annotation set available in Ensembl release 90.
source: Our data have been used by Ensembl to produce an updated gene annotation set, which is available in Ensembl release 90.
evidence: This states the outcome of data integration.

claim: Ensembl release 90 contains a total of 62,895 transcripts in 35,117 genes.
source: The new release contains a total of 62,895 transcripts in 35,117 genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the new annotation.

claim: 127 new protein-coding genes have been created as a consequence of incorporating the RNA-seq data.
source: 127 new protein-coding genes (Supplementary file 12) and 1166 new transcripts in previously annotated genes have been created as a consequence of incorporating our RNA-seq data (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the new annotation.

claim: 1166 new transcripts in previously annotated genes have been created as a consequence of incorporating the RNA-seq data.
source: 127 new protein-coding genes (Supplementary file 12) and 1166 new transcripts in previously annotated genes have been created as a consequence of incorporating our RNA-seq data (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the new annotation.

claim: The new protein-coding genes are expressed at lower levels (3-fold) on average as measured by their mean expression across the entire time course.
source: These genes are expressed at lower levels (3-fold) on average as measured by their mean expression across the entire time course (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), which may explain why they haven't previously been annotated.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the data.

claim: 5043 of the 35,117 genes show differential isoform usage across the time course.
source: We find that 5043 of the 35,117 genes show differential isoform usage across the time course (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary files 13–14) with 3084 genes expressing more than two isoforms across development (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from differential isoform analysis.

claim: 3084 genes express more than two isoforms across development.
source: We find that 5043 of the 35,117 genes show differential isoform usage across the time course (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary files 13–14) with 3084 genes expressing more than two isoforms across development (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from differential isoform analysis.

claim: 2294 new lincRNAs have been built by Ensembl using the data.
source: In addition, our data has been used by Ensembl, in conjunction with previously incorporated RNA-seq data, to build 2294 new lincRNAs (Supplementary file 12).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the new annotation.

claim: 1304 of the new lincRNAs are detected in the dataset with the same cut-off as for protein-coding genes.
source: Of these lincRNAs, 1304 are detected in our dataset with the same cut-off as for protein-coding genes (>0 TPM in all samples for at least one stage) and a high proportion show dynamic expression patterns across the 18 stages (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: 81 of the detectable lincRNAs have differential isoform usage during the time course.
source: Also, of the detectable lincRNAs, 81 have differential isoform usage during the time course.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from differential isoform analysis.

claim: The Ensembl lincRNAs have limited overlap with two previously published sets.
source: We compared the Ensembl lincRNAs with two previously published sets (Pauli et al., 2012; Ulitsky et al., 2011) to investigate the overlap. None of the sets overlap to any great extent, which possibly reflects the different methods and data that were used to identify them (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a result from comparative analysis.

claim: Only 10 of the e90 lincRNAs overlap lincRNAs in both of the other two sets.
source: Only 10 of the e90 lincRNAs overlap lincRNAs in both of the other two sets, one of which is malat1 (ENSDARG00000099970; Tripathi et al., 2010; Ulitsky et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from comparative analysis.

claim: The new lincRNAs tend to be shorter than protein-coding genes with fewer exons (mean length = 1006 nt, mean number of exons = 3.04).
source: Like mammalian and previously identified zebrafish lincRNAs (Cabili et al., 2011; Pauli et al., 2012; Ulitsky et al., 2011), they tend to be shorter than protein-coding genes with fewer exons (mean length = 1006 nt, mean number of exons = 3.04; Figure 7F–G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: lincRNAs are expressed at lower levels on average than protein-coding genes (protein-coding median = 7.3 TPM, lincRNA median = 1.6 TPM).
source: They are also expressed at lower levels on average (mean TPM across all samples; protein-coding, median = 7.3 TPM, lincRNA, median = 1.6 TPM; Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: The transcriptional start sites of lincRNAs are not well-defined.
source: Analysis of promoter-associated motifs shows that the transcriptional start sites of these genes are not well-defined (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C–D).
evidence: This is a result from motif analysis.

claim: The zebrafish lincRNA annotation relies on RNA-seq data only, therefore the inherent 3' bias of the expression data leads to less reliable 5' end annotation.
source: By contrast, the zebrafish lincRNA annotation relies on RNA-seq data only, therefore the inherent 3' bias of the expression data leads to less reliable 5' end annotation.
evidence: This is an explanation of a methodological limitation.

claim: miR-430 family is required for proper morphogenesis at early stages and oriented cell divisions in the neural rod.
source: As in other systems, miRNAs play important roles during zebrafish development such as the miR-430 family which is required for proper morphogenesis at early stages and also oriented cell divisions in the neural rod (Giraldez et al., 2005; Takacs and Giraldez, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Precursor hairpins (pre-miRNAs) are sliced from the host transcript in the nucleus by the microprocessor complex, consisting of the proteins Drosha (Rnasen) and Dgcr8 (Pasha).
source: First, precursor hairpins (pre-miRNAs) are sliced from the host transcript in the nucleus by the microprocessor complex, consisting of the proteins Drosha (Rnasen) and Dgcr8 (Pasha).
evidence: This describes the known miRNA processing pathway.

claim: The hairpin is cut by Dicer1 in the cytoplasm, freeing the miRNA duplex.
source: Subsequently the hairpin is cut by Dicer1 in the cytoplasm, freeing the miRNA duplex.
evidence: This describes the known miRNA processing pathway.

claim: The annotation of many primary miRNA genes is likely hindered by their rapid nuclear processing.
source: Although much effort has been dedicated to sequencing and annotating the mature miRNAs themselves, the annotation of many primary miRNA genes is likely hindered by their rapid nuclear processing (Chang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: RNA derived from dgcr8 and drosha wild-type, heterozygous and homozygous mutant embryos (5 dpf) was sequenced.
source: Reasoning that the depletion of drosha and dgcr8 may enrich the transcriptome for unprocessed pri-miRNAs, we sequenced RNA derived from dgcr8 and drosha wild-type, heterozygous and homozygous mutant embryos (5 dpf) to determine whether this would allow us to improve the current pri-miRNA annotation.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: The v87 Ensembl release includes 313 pri-miRNA transcripts overlapping 220 annotated miRNA loci.
source: The v87 release includes 313 pri-miRNA transcripts overlapping 220 annotated miRNA loci.
evidence: This is a quantitative description of the previous annotation.

claim: The assembly contains 398 pri-miRNA transcripts which overlap 283 miRNA loci, 94 of which are not currently associated with a pri-miRNA.
source: Our assembly contains 398 pri-miRNA transcripts which overlap 283 miRNA loci, 94 of which are not currently associated with a pri-miRNA (Figure 8A, Supplementary file 15–16).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the new assembly.

claim: The pri-miRNA transcripts are now available to view as a selectable track in Ensembl v90.
source: These pri-miRNA transcripts are now available to view as a selectable track in Ensembl v90 (Figure 8D).
evidence: This states the availability of the new annotation.

claim: Differential use of 3' ends can result in different/extra 3′ UTR sequence.
source: There are multiple possible consequences of alternative 3′ ends, such as different/extra 3′ UTR sequence (Figure 9A).
evidence: This describes a known consequence of alternative 3' end usage.

claim: Alternative 3′ ends can provide different binding sites for RNA-binding proteins or regulation by microRNAs.
source: This can provide different binding sites for RNA-binding proteins or regulation by microRNAs.
evidence: This describes a known consequence of alternative 3' end usage.

claim: Alternative 3′ ends can lead to different/extra coding sequence at the 3′ end of transcripts, leading to proteins that contain different domains.
source: Other possibilities include different/extra coding sequence at the 3′ end of transcripts, leading to proteins that contain different domains and can therefore fulfil different molecular functions.
evidence: This describes a known consequence of alternative 3' end usage.

claim: Alternative 3′ end usage was catalogued across development using a 3′ pulldown method called DeTCT.
source: We have catalogued alternative 3′ end usage across development for the same time points as the RNA-seq using a 3′ pulldown method called DeTCT (Collins et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the method used.

claim: Across all 423 samples over all the stages, there were 253,627 regions identified.
source: Across all 423 samples over all the stages (for each stage there are 11–12 replicates of pools of 8 embryos and 11–12 replicates of single embryos), there were 253,627 regions identified, where each region may be associated with multiple 3′ ends.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the DeTCT analysis.

claim: After filtering, the set was reduced to 37,724 regions.
source: Therefore, we have filtered these regions by various criteria such as distance to an annotated gene and genomic context to remove artefactual regions (Figure 9B, Figure 9—figure supplement 3 and Materials and methods), which reduces the set to 37,724 regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result after filtering.

claim: The stricter set contains 8358 regions.
source: For this analysis, we increased the stringency of filtering to reduce the inclusion of false-positive ends and produce a high-confidence set of 3′ ends to work from. This stricter set contains 8358 regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result after stricter filtering.

claim: 1552 genes have two or more 3′ ends.
source: Once the regions have been associated with annotated genes, 1552 genes have two or more 3′ ends (Supplementary file 18).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: pdlim5b has three alternative 3′ ends which are used at different times during development.
source: For example, pdlim5b (ENSDARG00000027600) has three alternative 3′ ends which are used at different times during development (Figure 9C–D).
evidence: This is a specific example from the data.

claim: During cleavage and gastrula stages, one particular end of pdlim5b is used (end 2).
source: During cleavage and gastrula stages, one particular end is used (end 2 in Figure 9C), but all three are observed during segmentation stages.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the data.

claim: All three ends of pdlim5b are observed during segmentation stages.
source: During cleavage and gastrula stages, one particular end is used (end 2 in Figure 9C), but all three are observed during segmentation stages.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the data.

claim: Ends 1 and 2 of pdlim5b would be predicted to produce the same protein with different 3′ UTRs.
source: Ends 1 and 2 would be predicted to produce the same protein with different 3′ UTRs, allowing for differential post-transcriptional regulation.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the data.

claim: End 3 of pdlim5b is predicted to produce a protein which lacks the C-terminal zinc finger domain.
source: However, end 3 is predicted to produce a protein which lacks the C-terminal zinc finger domain, allowing for this alternative transcript to have a completely different molecular function (Figure 9D).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the data.

claim: GO enrichment analysis of the 1552 genes with multiple 3' ends produces enrichments of a wide variety of biological processes with no obvious process or tissue specificity.
source: GO enrichment analysis of the 1552 genes with multiple 3' ends produces enrichments of a wide variety of biological processes from JNK signalling to exocrine pancreas development with no obvious process or tissue specificity (Supplementary file 19).
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: There are no enrichments for Pfam domains in genes with multiple 3' ends, suggesting that there isn't a particular class of gene that is more commonly regulated by alternative 3' ends.
source: There are no enrichments for Pfam domains, suggesting that there isn't a particular class of gene that is more commonly regulated by alternative 3' ends.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the enrichment analysis results.

claim: The large number of stages and replicates allows clustering of genes by their expression profile across all of development using a graph-based method.
source: The large number of stages and replicates allows us to cluster genes by their expression profile across all of development using a graph-based method.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach enabled by the data.

claim: The graph-based clustering splits the assayed genes into 254 different expression profiles containing at least five genes each.
source: This splits the assayed genes into 254 different expression profiles containing at least five genes each (11,439 of the genes are assigned to clusters).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: 11,439 of the genes are assigned to clusters.
source: This splits the assayed genes into 254 different expression profiles containing at least five genes each (11,439 of the genes are assigned to clusters).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: GO/ZFA enrichment on clusters allows suggestion of an association of unnamed genes with known processes.
source: GO/ZFA enrichment on these clusters allows us to suggest an association of unnamed genes with known processes.
evidence: This describes the utility of the enrichment analysis.

claim: There are many clusters which show no GO enrichments at all, despite having some well-known developmental regulators in them.
source: There are also many clusters which show no GO enrichments at all, despite having some well-known developmental regulators in them.
evidence: This is an observation from the enrichment analysis.

claim: Genes that already have GO annotations are more likely than unannotated genes to accrue new annotations leading to an inequality in annotation.
source: One possible explanation for this is that genes that already have GO annotations are more likely than unannotated genes to accrue new annotations leading to an inequality in annotation (Haynes et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The long arm of chromosome 4 is considered to be constitutive heterochromatin.
source: One intriguing set of clusters contains an over-representation of genes on the long arm of chromosome 4, a region considered to be constitutive heterochromatin (Howe et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The zinc finger genes on chromosome 4 may have a role during the activation of the zygotic genome.
source: Given this, it is tempting to speculate that these genes have a role during the activation of the zygotic genome.
evidence: This is speculation based on the expression pattern.

claim: In Drosophila the zinc finger gene Zelda (zld) is involved in zygotic genome activation by early and widespread binding to promoters and enhancers ahead of their genes' activation during the maternal-zygotic transition.
source: In Drosophila the zinc finger gene Zelda (zld) is involved in zygotic genome activation by early and widespread binding to promoters and enhancers ahead of their genes' activation during the maternal-zygotic transition (Harrison et al., 2010; Harrison et al., 2011; Liang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: In zebrafish, pou5f3, nanog and soxB genes have been implicated in activating specific genes during ZGA.
source: In zebrafish, pou5f3, nanog and soxB genes have been implicated in activating specific genes during ZGA (Lee et al., 2013; Leichsenring et al., 2013), but no general factor comparable to Zelda has been identified yet.
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: No general factor comparable to Zelda has been identified in zebrafish yet.
source: In zebrafish, pou5f3, nanog and soxB genes have been implicated in activating specific genes during ZGA (Lee et al., 2013; Leichsenring et al., 2013), but no general factor comparable to Zelda has been identified yet.
evidence: This states the current state of knowledge.

claim: The role of the ZnF protein family genes on chromosome 4 may be to set up or maintain open chromatin in a genome-wide way to allow for the rapid activation of the first zygotic genes.
source: It is possible that the role of the ZnF protein family genes on chromosome 4 is to set up or maintain open chromatin in a genome-wide way to allow for the rapid activation of the first zygotic genes.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data and biological knowledge.

claim: Clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135 contain four unnamed genes predicted to be H3K36 methyltransferases.
source: This is supported by the finding that these clusters also contain four unnamed genes, also found on chromosome 4, that are predicted to be H3K36 methyltransferases (ENSDARG00000104681, ENSDARG00000091062, ENSDARG00000076160, ENSDARG00000103283).
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: H3K36 methylation is generally associated with active euchromatin.
source: H3K36 methylation is generally, albeit not exclusively, associated with active euchromatin (Wagner and Carpenter, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of the chromatin modifier Kdm2aa leads to a specific de-repression of the ZnF genes on chromosome 4.
source: Notably, loss of the chromatin modifier Kdm2aa leads to a specific de-repression of these ZnF genes (Scahill et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The ZnF genes on chromosome 4 could be responsible for negatively regulating areas of open chromatin to stop inappropriate activation of transposable elements during ZGA.
source: Another option is that they could be responsible for negatively regulating areas of open chromatin to stop inappropriate activation of transposable elements during ZGA.
evidence: This is speculation based on biological knowledge.

claim: In mammals, suppression of retrotransposons is mediated by the rapidly evolving KRAB zinc finger genes.
source: In mammals, suppression of retrotransposons is mediated by the rapidly evolving KRAB zinc finger genes (Jacobs et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: KRAB zinc finger genes are not found in ray-finned fish.
source: KRAB zinc finger genes are not found in ray-finned fish (Imbeault et al., 2017), making the ZnF genes on chromosome 4 a possible functional equivalent.
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The ZnF genes on chromosome 4 may be a functional equivalent to KRAB zinc finger genes in ray-finned fish.
source: KRAB zinc finger genes are not found in ray-finned fish (Imbeault et al., 2017), making the ZnF genes on chromosome 4 a possible functional equivalent.
evidence: This is speculation based on comparative biology.

claim: Clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135 contain a large number of well-known developmental regulators such as members of the Tgf-beta (Bmp and Nodal) and Wnt signalling pathways.
source: Also, as would be expected given their expression profiles, within these four clusters are a large number of well-known developmental regulators such as members of the Tgf-beta (Bmp and Nodal) and Wnt signalling pathways, as well as transcription factors such as gata5 & 6, sox32, vox, ved, vent and both Brachyury homologues.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: Clusters 7, 23, 26 and 135 contain transcription factors such as gata5 & 6, sox32, vox, ved, vent and both Brachyury homologues.
source: Also, as would be expected given their expression profiles, within these four clusters are a large number of well-known developmental regulators such as members of the Tgf-beta (Bmp and Nodal) and Wnt signalling pathways, as well as transcription factors such as gata5 & 6, sox32, vox, ved, vent and both Brachyury homologues.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: Although there is a skew towards positive temporal expression correlation among paralogues, a significant proportion have diverged in their expression pattern as demonstrated by low or negative correlation coefficients.
source: Correlation analysis of paralogues stemming from a teleost-specific genome duplication shows that although there is the expected skew towards positive temporal expression correlation, a significant proportion of paralogues have diverged in their expression pattern as demonstrated by low or negative correlation coefficients.
evidence: This is a result from correlation analysis.

claim: Some genes have expression patterns that are diverged spatially, but not temporally.
source: It will also be the case that some genes have expression patterns that are diverged spatially, but not temporally and we will not necessarily be able to detect these events.
evidence: This is a limitation of the temporal-only analysis.

claim: The phenomenon of divergence is widespread among paralogues.
source: Thus, the number of genes whose expression annotations do not overlap is an estimate, but it does suggest that the phenomenon of divergence is widespread among paralogues, something that might be expected to be the case since there needs to be some form of selective pressure on retaining paralogous pairs.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data and evolutionary reasoning.

claim: GO enrichment of highly correlated paralogues reveals a skew towards neural and muscle expression.
source: GO enrichment of highly correlated paralogues reveals a skew towards neural and muscle expression whereas negatively correlated pairs do not exhibit this expression restriction, which is likely to reflect greater GO term diversity among the latter.
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Negatively correlated paralogous pairs do not exhibit expression restriction to neural and muscle, which is likely to reflect greater GO term diversity.
source: GO enrichment of highly correlated paralogues reveals a skew towards neural and muscle expression whereas negatively correlated pairs do not exhibit this expression restriction, which is likely to reflect greater GO term diversity among the latter.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GO enrichment results.

claim: The data have added 127 previously unknown potential protein-coding genes to Ensembl's annotation.
source: Our data has added 127 previously unknown potential protein-coding genes to Ensembl's annotation.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the annotation update.

claim: The new protein-coding genes are expressed at lower levels on average and many are expressed in a limited number of stages, which may explain why there has not been enough evidence previously for Ensembl's gene-build pipeline to annotate them.
source: These genes are expressed at lower levels on average than the entire set of protein-coding genes and many are expressed in a limited number of stages. This may explain why there has not been enough evidence previously for Ensembl's gene-build pipeline to annotate them.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why these genes were not previously annotated.

claim: 7821 lincRNAs are currently annotated in Ensembl for the human genome.
source: Similarly, 2294 new genes annotated as lincRNAs have been added. This compares with 7821 currently annotated in Ensembl for the human genome.
evidence: This is a comparison with human annotation.

claim: The fact that there is so little overlap between the three lincRNA sets is probably because of the different methods that were used to define them.
source: The fact that there is so little overlap between the three sets is probably because of the different methods that were used to define them.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the limited overlap.

claim: The numbers of transcripts produced by the Ensembl pipeline suggest that it is more sensitive, but less specific than the other two methods.
source: The numbers of transcripts produced by the Ensembl pipeline suggest that it is more sensitive, but less specific than the other two methods.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison of methods.

claim: Incorporation of CAGE data would help to correctly identify the 5' ends of lincRNA transcripts.
source: Incorporation of CAGE data would also help to correctly identify the 5' ends of these transcripts.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future improvement.

claim: The involvement of microRNAs during embryonic development is widespread.
source: The involvement of microRNAs during embryonic development is widespread (reviewed in Bartel, 2009; Mishima, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to reviews.

claim: The primary transcripts of miRNAs are often poorly annotated.
source: However, the primary transcripts of miRNAs are often poorly annotated.
evidence: This states a known limitation in annotation.

claim: Using two miRNA processing mutants (dgcr8 and drosha), an improved pri-miRNA assembly was produced with an increase of 42% in the number of Ensembl miRNAs with an associated primary transcript.
source: Using two miRNA processing mutants (dgcr8 and drosha), we have produced an improved pri-miRNA assembly with an increase of 42% in the number of Ensembl miRNAs with an associated primary transcript, including genes implicated in developmental processes in zebrafish (Figure 9D, Fan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the pri-miRNA assembly.

claim: The assembly shows that miRNAs are processed from primary transcripts with multiple isoforms with potentially multiple transcription start sites.
source: In agreement with previous studies (Chang et al., 2015; Gaeta et al., 2017), the assembly shows that miRNAs are processed from primary transcripts with multiple isoforms with potentially multiple transcription start sites (Figure 9).
evidence: This is supported by citations and shown in the data.

claim: The diversity of pri-miRNA transcripts means that the expression of miRNAs in relatively close proximity could be regulated at multiple levels.
source: This diversity of transcripts means that the expression of miRNAs in relatively close proximity (e.g. dre-let-7d-1 and dre-mir-125a-1) could be regulated at multiple levels (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of transcript diversity.

claim: It is possible that a proportion of the assembled pri-miRNA constructs are fragments.
source: It is possible that a proportion of the assembled constructs are fragments.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the assembly.

claim: Clear definition of the 5' and 3' termini of pri-miRNAs will require further work and ultimately experimental validation by an alternative method such as 5′ rapid amplification of cDNA ends.
source: Clear definition of the 5' and 3' termini will require further work and ultimately experimental validation by an alternative method such as 5′ rapid amplification of cDNA ends.
evidence: This suggests future work needed for validation.

claim: The dataset uncovers new splice isoforms that show differential expression across the 18 stages.
source: A further layer of complexity is added by differential exon and 3′ end use. The dataset uncovers new splice isoforms that show differential expression across the 18 stages.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis.

claim: When viewed in Ensembl against the Ensembl genebuild, the data refine the current gene annotation and tie splice isoforms to their temporal expression patterns.
source: When viewed in Ensembl against the Ensembl genebuild, this refines the current gene annotation and ties splice isoforms to their temporal expression patterns.
evidence: This describes the utility of the data for annotation.

claim: One possible explanation for phenotypic discrepancies between morpholino knockdown and mutations is that mutations affect potentially non-critical exons that are only present in a subset of transcripts of a given gene.
source: One possible explanation for phenotypic discrepancies between morpholino antisense oligo knockdown, code disrupting point mutations and CRISPR/Cas9 or TALEN-mediated larger deletions is that mutations affect potentially non-critical exons that are only present in a subset of transcripts of a given gene.
evidence: This is an interpretation relevant to the ongoing debate about reverse genetics approaches.

claim: Genes carrying code-disrupting mutations created by ENU or CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis can produce potentially functional transcripts by exon skipping.
source: Indeed, recent publications demonstrate that genes carrying code-disrupting mutations created by ENU or CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis can produce potentially functional transcripts by exon skipping (Anderson et al., 2017; Mou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: An improved annotation that gives temporal resolution of exon usage is of great value for the identification of critical exons.
source: An improved annotation that gives temporal resolution of exon usage is of great value for the identification of critical exons.
evidence: This states the value of the improved annotation.

claim: In accordance with previous work, differential use of not only 3′ UTRs but also coding sequence across development was found.
source: Using the 3′ end sequencing method DeTCT, we have catalogued the differential use of alternative 3′ ends in a filtered set of transcripts. In accordance with previous work on a subset of stages (Collins et al., 2012; Sheppard et al., 2013; Ulitsky et al., 2012) we find that there is differential use of not only 3′ UTRs but also coding sequence across development.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: pdlim5b is expressed as several transcripts, with a single maternal isoform and multiple zygotic ones which would be predicted to produce different proteins.
source: We show that pdlim5b is expressed as several transcripts, with a single maternal isoform and multiple zygotic ones which would be predicted to produce different proteins.
evidence: This is a specific example from the data.

claim: This type of data provides scope for temporally resolved analysis using transcript-specific knockout targeting strategies.
source: This type of data provides scope for temporally resolved analysis using transcript-specific knockout targeting strategies.
evidence: This states the potential application of the data.

claim: A major aim for this work was to create an accessible reference of normal mRNA expression during zebrafish development.
source: A major aim for this work was to create an accessible reference of normal mRNA expression during zebrafish development.
evidence: This states the aim of the work.

claim: The primary sequence is available from the European Nucleotide Archive.
source: The primary sequence is available from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA, http://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena), but importantly has also been interpreted for immediate user-friendly access.
evidence: This states where the data can be accessed.

claim: Pre-computed analyses allow an in-depth examination of the data on a gene by gene basis.
source: These pre-computed analyses allow an in-depth examination of the data on a gene by gene basis.
evidence: This describes the utility of the pre-computed analyses.

claim: The data make it easy for researchers to benefit from the dataset and provide a direct link to the wealth of information present in genomic databases.
source: This makes it easy for researchers to benefit from the data and provides a direct link to the wealth of information present in genomic databases.
evidence: This states the benefit of data accessibility.
